surfaces.reason: OCaml applies and validates session-updating forms on load; TypeScript stores parsed source.
The OCaml host has no equivalent of the TypeScript inferAuthoritySource/checkAuthority API.

TypeScript preserves its declaration wrappers and session/source summaries in a versioned v1 envelope. Declaration hashes use SHA-256 over sorted-key canonical JSON; OCaml uses MD5 and serialization order. Shared fixtures compare payloads, provenance, module identities and type summaries, plus 58-source/548-declaration corpus kind/module counts. TypeScript omits OCaml artifact-cache telemetry and returns validation failures from artifactSummary rather than aggregating failing sources.
surfaces.typescript: language-ts-artifact/v1; sha256 over canonical JSON with sorted object keys
surfaces.ocaml: CanonicalIr v1; md5 over serialized declaration payloads

surfaces.reason: identifySyntax is implemented by the TypeScript host only. It depends on the shared reader grammar; the OCaml hosts do not expose it yet.
Per-expression observation (evaluate observe) is implemented by the TypeScript VM and evaluator only. The OCaml hosts ignore the observe field.
symbolIndex and findReferences are implemented by the TypeScript host only; they use the TypeScript expander and descriptor parser.
applyEditScript, describeNodes, and editScriptSchema are implemented by the TypeScript host only. Scripts are engine-neutral data over the shared reader grammar.
sourceToOutline and outlineToSource are implemented by the TypeScript host only. They depend only on the shared reader grammar.
formSlots is implemented by the TypeScript host only; it reads descriptors with the TypeScript descriptor parser.

The language server and editors run the TypeScript analysis workspace (docs/rfcs/0004-one-analysis-architecture.md). The OCaml editorAnalyze, editorHover, editorCompletion, editorDefinition, and editorFormat ops have no JavaScript consumer and are not compared.
The TypeScript reader reads nil as a symbol named nil; the OCaml reader produces a distinct nil node. The effect-ir projections agree (both emit Var nil).

Neither HM typechecker accepts the Effect program forms (define-layer, define-class, combinators, typed defines); both reject them with different diagnostics. Effect programs are checked by the mechanics checker, so only effect-typescript/operational-effects compares typecheck.

TypeScript runs registered canonical payload schemas for every ontology kind, named validators, descriptor contracts and HTTP checks; Effect Schema diagnostic wording and nested span precision differ from OCaml.
